Sleep Wednesday May 22

https://osmand.net/go?lat=38.38102&lon=-93.755424

This is a baseball dugout, for those who know little about baseball.

They are very common and can be found in communities across America. 

They are often found to be a great place to take refuge during a storm or to spend the night.

Look for them always when free camping and crossing America by bicycle.

Here is a general idea of what people must pay for food and drinks at a typical 2020 American small community baseball game.

Hamburger, chips and a drink for 5 dollars.

Snapshot in time.

Rules of the trail ... thus far, I believe this Katy Trail may be the highlight of this cross country American journey.

Already I am seeing it as a social experience and a great way to meet people.

It is a well developed tourist attraction, and  now is just the very beginning of the season.
There are great, informative billboard graphics everywhere. I am at the west terminus now.

I slept in the Clinton area last night, behind the community center.

American states are composed of counties, and each county has a town, city or village called the county seat.

The county seat is where the sheriff and the main court house is located.

This is also where legal documents are recorded and stored.

The county seat is also often the center for the annual county fair, and there will often always be a county fairgrounds in the area.

Such fairgrounds are often good places to free camp.

Last night, I found this site for camping, which was behind the community center in Clinton.

The men's room was unlocked, very large and clean, and there was power and hot water.

A severe storm was in progress and one could not have found a better place to stay.

Another cyclist had already occupied the bathroom before I arrived, but I found a tent outside to be best.
Classic Missouri barn scene.
Missouri welcomes you ...

Slept on the front porch of an abandoned farm house right along the trail.

The home is fast deteriorating but all locked up tight. There are several out buildings. Very quiet with no neighbors or roads nearby.

In most other places in the world, this home would have been broken into, stripped of everything and left open.

The place is probably for sale.

Upon reaching the Missouri River, I've found many sections of the Katy Trail to be flooded with no alternative route.

The flooding continues to worsen as the rains continue. Water is flowing down from Nebraska to the Mississippi River valley along the Missouri River valley causing flooding, road closings and power outages.

Right now I am in Columbia, Missouri, safe and dry in an abandoned McMansion. 

At this point, when sunshine does return, I may need to alter my route away from the Katy Trail and take US route 40 to Pittsburgh.

This is Missouri, a little like Kansas. Many, many Christian billboards.
An incredible auto salvage yard.  180 acres of land, including 45 acres of autos. 9000 autos.

I spoke long and deep with the owner. Eddie is 67 and recently had a knee operation. He's been at the salvage business for 45 years. He wants to convert to an online sales operation, so I left him my contact information.
Found this knife on the road side later in the day.
I gave it away to another cyclist. It was very heavy, not necessary.

Another divorce with kids, with quick evacuation, leaving much good food behind in the kitchen. A very horrible place and ugly situation.

I'm beginning to understand the bigger problem of what is happening in America today through examining not only their general refuse, but the aftermath of suspended family lifestyles.

Not a great place to sleep or hang out, but I was sheltered from a rain storm.

I'm thankful for my life and outlook.
